chapter: Money, touring and the loud horn
title: Memphis excursion dance that paid Punch five hundred dollars
summary: Punch tells how he took a share of the gate instead of salary for a Memphis dance and made about $550.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So if he ain't got it now he'll never get it. That's for sure. And never forget I went to Memphis on an excursion from Chicago with a band. I had the band and they had five pieces. And a fella named Robert Henry had the outfit. And he asked each man in the band. He said uh now we're going in Memphis to a dance hall. And he said uh I think we're going to do good. He said now would y'all like to go in with the dance or just want a salary? And every one of them wanted a salary. They wanted twelve dollars a man for playing that night. He said well okay. So he said Poncha. He said well you just wake along with us. I said okay. I didn't care if I make a thing or not. I was drinking my liquor and doing a thing about it. And they had a great big yard full of something across the street before you get in the hall. All around the hall. And they're paying a dollar head at the gate. At the door. And did you know the yard was packed and jammed over seven hundred people and the hall was three hundred and something. About a dollar head. And he paid them all. And told him, now y'all got your own money. So now I got to do business with Poncha. I told you about that didn't you? Yeah. And I got five hundred and something out of it. Then I didn't get as much as I was supposed to get. But I got five hundred and about fifty dollars. Thank God. Oh my. For one night.
